Comparison

TPO vs. EPDM

Side-by-side comparison of the two most common single-ply commercial membranes — performance, cost, longevity, and which conditions favor each.

Template — not yet published Updated July 1, 2026 1 min read Editorial standards · Report an error
Template — not yet publishedThis page demonstrates a template structure. It is not editorial content and must not be read as guidance.

Key takeaways

  • Neither membrane 'wins' universally — climate, building use, and budget determine the better fit.
  • White TPO typically outperforms in cooling-dominated climates; black EPDM in heating-dominated ones.
  • EPDM has a longer field-performance track record; TPO formulations have improved but vary by manufacturer.
  • Installation quality dominates brand choice in both systems.

How this comparison was built

Criteria were fixed before evaluation and applied identically to both systems, per the CRI Methodology. Sources include ASTM standards, manufacturer technical data sheets, and field-performance research — not marketing.

Side by side

CriterionTPOEPDM
Typical service life15–25 years20–30 years
Seam methodHot-air weldedAdhesive/tape
Solar reflectivityHigh (white)Low (black; white available)
Track record~30 years, evolving formulations50+ years, stable chemistry
Typical installed costPlaceholder rangePlaceholder range
Best-fit climateCooling-dominatedHeating-dominated
